title: Kernel Hive canonical tile registry entry

listing.description: SOFT HIDE — whether this exhibit is announced in the gallery's listings. Absent means listed, so every entry without this block behaves exactly as before. `hidden` keeps the tile a full lineup entry in every other respect (it still ships in gallery-manifest.json, still streams, still keeps its scene bindings and poster) and only removes it from the grid, the 3D hall and their counts. It is DISCOVERABILITY, NOT ACCESS CONTROL: /os/<id> still resolves and streams, so anyone with the URL gets in. To retire an exhibit from the lineup, use `enabled: false` instead.

state.description: There is deliberately no separate `dark` state: a never-announced dark launch and a temporarily-withdrawn exhibit render identically everywhere, so the difference lives in `reason` (prose a human reads) rather than in an enum value no consumer could branch on.

reason.description: Required when hidden, forbidden when listed. Why it is off the floor, and what would put it back. `git log -- registry/stations/<id>.json` answers who took it off.

since.description: Required when hidden, forbidden when listed. The date it came off the floor, so a stale hide is visible as a stale hide.

pointer.description: How a visitor's pointer reaches this guest. `transport`/`backend` name the DAEMON's delivery route (streamhost SH_POINTER / SH_INPUT_BACKEND); `method`/`absolute`/`present` name what the GUEST actually gets, and are cross-checked against the route, the device ledger and operator.labctl.pointer_mode by validate_pointer_method() in scripts/stations-registry.py.

method.description: The mechanism that puts the pointer where the visitor pointed. Finer wire detail is carried by existing siblings, not by extra enum values: `backend` separates mamecmd from mamesock, `agentAddress` separates a warpd agent on a hostfwd TCP port from one on a serial chardev. See registry/README.md for one sentence and an example tile per value.

absolute.description: The guest receives the visitor's position, not motion deltas. Mirrors InputBackend::pointer_mode() in streamhost/streamhost/src/config/backends.rs: true for every backend but dbus-rel and disabled.

present.description: Any pointer input at all reaches the guest. false is the keyboard-only exhibit (SH_INPUT_BACKEND=disabled) and the showcase poster.

emulator.description: WHICH emulator produces this station's pixels, declared once here because nothing else in the repo records it machine-readably (QEMU/MAME/VICE/… versions live in build-script pins and prose). For a Tier-2 bridge station this is the emulator INSIDE the kiosk, not the QEMU that hosts the kiosk (that is runtime.qemu.binary). Required for every production entry; rendered into fleet-table.json for the SPA's /fleet view.

family.description: Product name: QEMU, MAME, VICE, Hatari, Open SIMH, es40, … `none` for a poster with no runtime.

version.description: String or null (the schema evaluator has no type unions; validate_rules.validate_emulator enforces it). Release or pin the box actually runs ("0.289", "11.0.2", a short commit). null = not recorded anywhere in the repo yet — the table shows the gap instead of a guess.

source.description: Where the pin lives / how the binary was built (script path, package, fork).

driver.description: The emulated machine inside the emulator, where the family alone is ambiguous (MAME driver, VICE binary, QEMU -M).

keyboard.description: How this MACHINE's keyboard differs from a PC's. Consumed by the SPA typist and by labctl (via SH_KEY_MAP in station.env). Derive it with scripts/dev/mame-keymap.py.

charMap.description: Guest character -> the host character whose keystroke produces it.

letterCase.description: upper-only: the machine has no lower case and its shifted letter row is symbols, so letters must be sent unshifted.

demoProgram.description: Optional type-in listing the SPA can type into this guest (stage menu → 'Type in a demo program').

perCharMs.description: Milliseconds one character takes to REACH this guest, i.e. the rate streamhost drains the typed queue at (SH_KEY_MIN_HOLD_MS + SH_KEY_MIN_GAP_MS). The SPA typist waits line.length * this before submitting the next line; underestimating it grows a backlog and BASIC loses characters. Omit to accept the SPA default (DEMO_PER_CHAR_MS); validation requires whichever applies to be >= hold+gap.

ui.description: What kind of interface the exhibited scene IS, so the fleet table can answer 'graphical desktop or not' (nothing else records it: reset.mouse is a test status and the fixture prose is not parseable). desktop = windowing GUI (incl. GEOS/GEM/Workbench on 8-bit/16-bit machines); text-console = an OS shell or login on a text screen; home-computer = an 8-bit power-on BASIC/monitor screen; mobile = phone UI; other = anything else (gt40 vector-display game). Required for production entries.

network.description: OPTIONAL hand-declared truth about the GUEST's networking, for the cases the QEMU device ledger cannot answer (fleet_table.py derives NIC/backend/hostfwd from runtime.qemu for everything else): a NIC the guest never configured, a pcap/veth path outside QEMU, two VMs talking to each other, or 'none, deliberately'. Only declare it when the ledger would mislead; a declared block overrides the derived status in fleet-table.json and is labelled as declared.

status.description: internet: guest reaches out (NAT/SLIRP or masquerade). host-only: guest and host talk, no egress. isolated: link up, nothing reachable (e.g. SLIRP restrict=on). nic-only: a NIC exists but the guest has no IP configured. none: no network device at all.

note.description: The mechanism and where it is documented.

retronet.description: OPTIONAL hand-declared membership of the OFFLINE retronet bridge vmbr-rn (docs/lab/RETRONET-BRIEF.md). Present iff the guest's NIC is enslaved to that bridge; absent means 'not on the retronet'. It declares only the BRIDGE facts — the ICQ persona (uin/nick/client/onboarded) stays single-sourced in scripts/retronet/icq/roster.json and is merged in by fleet_table.py, never duplicated here. Cross-validated by stations-registry.py: addresses are unique and inside 10.99.0.0/24, the icq plane and the roster must agree in BOTH directions, and doc must exist.

planes.description: Which retronet planes this guest participates in. web = a period browser reads the corpus web off the gateway's :80 origin. icq = an OSCAR client signs into the gateway's :5190 ICQ service; declaring it REQUIRES a roster row in scripts/retronet/icq/roster.json (and every onboarded roster row requires this plane).

address.description: The guest's address on the bridge. Unique across the fleet; 10.99.0.2 is the gateway CT and 10.99.0.1 the labhost side, so neither is assignable. Omit if not recorded.

addressing.description: How the guest gets that address: a retronet-dhcp reservation, or hand-configured in the guest. Omit if not recorded.

link.description: The HOST-side link into the bridge, e.g. 'tap winxprn0 on vmbr-rn' or 'veth tru64-h/tru64-g (pcap) on vmbr-rn'.

guard.description: The per-station fail-closed iptables INPUT chain that contains the guest, e.g. WINXPRN-IN. Omit if not recorded.

joined.description: The date the station joined the bridge. Omit if not recorded.

doc.description: Repo-relative path of the station's primary retronet doc. Must exist.
